articles.title: Pierre Sage insists players and Crystal Palace hierarchy still support him despite poor start to season
articles.summary: Under-pressure Crystal Palace head coach Pierre Sage on his future after 2-0 home defeat to Newcastle: "The noise around the team and club is only noise, it's normal [to be under pressure] because we don't have the results"
articles.body:
The Eagles were soundly beaten at Selhurst Park on Sunday as they failed to bounce back from last weekend's 5-0 hammering at Brighton, with an 11-minute double from the Magpies shortly after half-time sealing their fate.

The timing of the goals - the first coming barely a minute after the restart following Sage's half-time team talk - was particularly concerning with Palace again starting a half slowly. A fifth of Palace's goals conceded have come in the first 10 minutes of games this season, including three in the heavy defeat at the Amex Stadium last weekend.

But when asked whether he thought he retained the belief of his players and the club hierarchy, he said: "Yes. I think they do [believe in me].

"It's normal [to be under pressure] because we don't have the results. The noise is a consequence of the team and we don't have [the points] we expect.

"Inside, we just are really focused on the solutions, how to be better and how to create the conditions to compete. I don't have to convince people around the club, I just have to convince the players to do their best and continue their improvement.

"After that, this kind of decision of what we are speaking about is to the chairman and owners. For me, the noise around the team and club is only noise.

"I spoke with the chairman this week, but I didn't speak about this subject.

"We spoke about the game, the condition of the team and how we build our game plan to compete today. We didn't speak about this subject. I share my strategy with him and the technical staff. It's normal."

Sage led Lens to their first ever French Cup last season in his one and only season in charge at the club, as well as a runners-up spot in Ligue 1, but has struggled to adapt as quickly to life in the Premier League with Palace only two points ahead of bottom side Sunderland with eight games gone.

The Frenchman admitted he had expected his start to be better but insisted things would improve given time.

"I always expected to do better," he said. "Football is an imperfect game, there's a lot of mistakes - players and coaches. It's always a frustration if you don't achieve the perfect thing.

"In my position, I just have to create the conditions to be close to perfection with the team in concentration, defending well, attacking well.

"But for the moment, we missed our game in Brighton. But today we missed only 15 minutes, but that's enough for the opponent to win. "

Sage believes Palace will have to be better at keeping the ball to arrest their poor defensive record, which has seen them ship 19 goals in the Premier League so far - the most in the league.

But that may raise further questions about his squad's ability to adapt to his methods, given the club has the third-lowest average possession percentage across the division so far.

He said: "My way, my idea is that the best way to defend is about having the ball, because if you have it you can't concede. But there are other ways to concede fewer goals.

"I just have to find the solution and I think today, it was not a tactical problem, it was a mental problem because when we came back from the dressing room we let our opponent do too many things.

"When you don't master the ball, when you don't control the play, you give the initiative to the opponent. When you have it and concede in transition, the problem is different.

"Today, and from the beginning [of the season], we have a lack of mastering the ball as a team and during the first half we created our chances in the transition, but didn't have possession.

"In the second half it was different, when they scored the second they played lower and in this situation we didn't have too many situations where we could concede. That's why I think it's the best way."

articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini comparecía en sala de prensa tras el empate sin goles de su equipo en la visita al Celta de Vigo. El técnico del Betis cree que fue "un empate justo". "Ellos fueron superiores en el primer tiempo. No hicimos una buena primera parte ni con balón. Tuvieron un par de jugadas peligrosas tan claras como las dos nuestras. En términos generales, si analizamos los 90 minutos, creo que un punto es justo para cada uno. Un tiempo para ellos y otro para nosotros". Aunque se generaron ocasiones de gol por parte de ambos equipos, "lamentablemente no siempre puede haber goles, pero son dos equipos que juegan a ganar. Tratan de darle prioridad a la parte técnica y son más de construcción que de destrucción. Fue un partido entretenido y con llegadas ambas porterías". Pellegrini apostó de inicio por Deossa como delantero. "No quería tirar antes de Parrott. Ellos juegan con tres centrales y se trataba de llegar desde segunda línea, pero no tuvimos mucho volumen ofensivo. Troy viene de jugar con su selección cuatro partidos en tres semana y hay que dosificarlo. Igual la pregunta no hubiera sido la misma si entra el tiro de Deossa. En términos generales, el equipo rindió dentro de lo esperado", comentó el chileno. Dos nombres propios para finalizar. Primero, Ceballos. "Dani, en la medida que se va poniendo a punto, va teniendo más minutos y eso le va a dar mejor rendimiento. Fornals y Fidalgo entraron muy bien también. Es un puesto que está bien cubierto", apuntó. articles.title: Michael Carrick Man Utd future: Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann expected frontrunners if head coach departs
articles.summary: Man Utd beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford to heap the pressure on head coach Michael Carrick; Captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped and United are eight games without a win
articles.body:
United plunged to a new low on Sunday as they were beaten 3-0 at Old Trafford by Bournemouth . The defeat extends their winless run to eight matches and leaves United just above the Premier League relegation zone.

Sky Sports News understands that United's bosses were already considering alternatives for the head coach role even before the defeat to Bournemouth amid the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

The United hierachy will now accelerate that process, with an expectation from insiders at the club that Carrick will be relieved of his duties.

That decision will ultimately come down to director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada, who will make a recommendation to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Carragher calls for quick decision as fearful Neville predicts sacking

Carrick's position looked to have become untenable as Bournemouth stormed to a deserved victory on Sunday in which United were a distant second-best. With captain Bruno Fernandes benched for the duration of the game following his midweek criticism of Carrick's tactics, United were fortunate to only lose by three goals.

"It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That's the problem the club have got," said Neville during Sky Sports' match commentary. On his podcast, Neville concluded: "They are probably going to sack him. Tomorrow, they will probably make a decision that will disgust Manchester United fans but it is probably necessary."

"Michael Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties tonight," added Jamie Carragher. "Not just for the good of Manchester United but also for the good of Michael Carrick. It has become untenable."

Who are the contenders to replace Carrick?

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett and Dan Khan:

If Carrick is to depart, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe are the two front runners to take over at Old Trafford. Both are available to start quickly, and neither would require any compensation to be paid. Howe, when he resigned as Newcastle manager in July, said he wanted to take a break from football to recharge his batteries. But Sky Sports News has been told he would be interested in talking to United, should a vacancy become available.

Howe was recommended by United's former sporting director Dan Ashworth as a suitable candidate in the past, having got to know him well during his time at Newcastle. Wilcox, United's current director of football, is thought to favour hiring a coach with Premier League experience.

Nagelsmann is well known to United's head of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, after the two men worked closely together at RB Leipzig. The former Bayern Munich boss has been out of work since stepping down as Germany head coach following a disastrous World Cup which saw the side knocked out by Paraguay in the round of 32 in the summer.

Unai Emery and Antonio Conte have also been considered by United as possible replacements, but they aren't thought to be among the current favourites. Emery, we have been told, remains committed to the project at Aston Villa.

However, Carragher believes Aston Villa's Unai Emery should be United's first target.

"He is a manager I look at when I think about Manchester United," said Carragher. "I think Emery is the best manager in the Premier League. But I've got this thing with him. Yes, his record in the Europa League is amazing, but surely somebody who is that successful wants to be known in the Champions League.

"He wants to win the Champions League. He's not going to do that at Aston Villa.

"He's had two experiences that haven't gone particularly well for him, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal. And I just think surely he would want that opportunity to prove himself at an absolute giant of a football club. Sorry, Villa fans."

Image: Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Unai Emery and Antonio Conte

articles.title: Jordan FA chief says AFC Congress ‘pure politics’ at behest of Infantino
articles.summary: Prince Ali bin Hussein said nobody was allowed to speak, question, debate or talk to the media at the AFC Congress.
articles.body:
The head of Jordan’s Football Association (JFA), Prince Ali bin Hussein, has accused FIFA President Gianni Infantino of hijacking the Asian Football Confederation Congress for political purposes ahead of his re-election bid for a fourth term.

At the AFC’s extraordinary congress in Tokyo on Friday, its president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al-Khalifa endorsed Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president.

Months after the confederation accused Infantino of a “fundamental breach of trust” over the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal , Sheikh Salman told the congress that Asia was now united behind Infantino .

But JFA’s Prince Ali, who has been a vocal critic of FIFA’s leadership, painted a starkly different picture of events in Tokyo.

“Having come back from Tokyo where the AFC Congress took place, the first two days were about football, which we all serve. The last day was pure politics at the behest of Gianni Infantino,” Prince Ali wrote on X.

“There were reports that Asia has a united position when it comes to electing the next FIFA President. In fact, nobody was allowed to speak, question, debate or talk with the media.

“Lack of transparency leads to lack of accountability. No amount of coercion, threats or bribes should be allowed.”

Prince Ali did not elaborate on his statement.

Al Jazeera reached out to FIFA and the AFC for a comment but had not received a response at the time of publication.

Infantino also addressed the AFC Congress, giving Sheikh Salman his backing for another term.

In August, Prince Ali launched a public attack on Infantino, accusing him of “blackmail” and saying FIFA had offered to help solve the kingdom’s problems in exchange for his endorsement.

Two days later, Prince Ali confirmed Jordan’s players and staff had received outstanding reward money for their participation in the 2025 Arab Cup.

The association had been waiting since December for prize money for reaching the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

On Saturday, Infantino laughed off questions about whether he had considered resigning in the wake of the failed FFE proposal, pointing to what he described as overwhelming support from member associations around the globe.

The Swiss-Italian administrator’s re-election prospects were strengthened significantly after the AFC endorsement, leaving Europe increasingly isolated and exposing the lack of a challenger.

articles.title: AP College Football Poll 2026 Week 9 Rankings Released with Top Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: The upper portion of the Associated Press Top 25 poll once again looks a little different with two teams unbeaten no more.
articles.body:
The upper portion of the Associated Press Top 25 poll once again looks a little different with two teams unbeaten no more.

BYU dropped from second to No. 8 after losing 39-31 to UCF in overtime, while Texas Tech slipped to 13th following a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati.

Texas, on the other hand, earned a big 34-27 win over previously No. 7 Ole Miss but threw away a 21-point lead in the process. As a result, the Longhorns jumped eight places to 11th.

Unranked CFB teams cause chaos in Week 8

It's too early to know if Texas' victory means anything bigger for Steve Sarkisian's squad.

Arch Manning provided another clunker. The fourth-year quarterback went 18-of-30 for 212 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Star wide receiver Cam Coleman was limited to one reception.

But the defense bowed up when it needed to and intercepted three passes by Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss.

At the very least, it's hard to argue Texas is totally fixed when these second-half swoons have become such a trend.

Even more confounding is the Big 12 title race.

Utah is the only team with a perfect conference record now, while BYU, Arizona, Texas Tech and Oklahoma State are all tied at 3-1.

The Red Raiders experienced perhaps the single biggest reversal of fortunes from the group on Saturday. They went from a 6-0 team with a straightforward path to the College Football Playoff to one that needs to rebuild its stock a bit without a lot of chances to notch a statement victory. Arizona is the highest-ranked team left on the schedule.

Oh, and mega booster Cody Campbell is posting cryptically on social media:

BYU, on the other hand, can still hang its hat on the 28-24 win over Notre Dame, and taking down in-state rival Utah on Nov. 7 will impress the CFP selection committee if it happens.

What might prove to be one of the more consequential outcomes didn't shake up the Top 25 very much.

USC put up just seven points and 241 yards of offense while getting upset by unranked Wisconsin. The Badgers, meanwhile, came out on top despite quarterback Colton Joseph throwing for 58 yards on 14 attempts.

Firing coach Lincoln Riley at this point probably wouldn't change much, and he does have an opportunity to salvage the season. Running the table would mean beating Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA.

Five years into Riley's tenure, however, the Trojans aren't in a meaningfully better position than they were under Clay Helton. A coaching change would be expensive , but the status quo is proving costly in its own way.

articles.title: Liverpool beat Brighton: Alexander Isak living up to price tag as Liverpool's winning run continues
articles.summary: Alexander Isak scores his sixth Premier League goal of the season as Liverpool make it four wins out of their last four under Andoni Iraola.
articles.body:
It has been a long time coming but Alexander Isak might finally be living up to his price tag.

The Sweden striker arrived at Anfield amid huge fanfare in August 2025 when he signed from Newcastle for a British record £125m.

But a combination of a slow start and then suffering a broken leg in December meant his first season at the Reds became something of a nightmare - scoring just four goals in 22 games.

This season has been a different story. Isak's goal against Brighton on Sunday helped Liverpool to an impressive 2-0 win against the Premier League's in-form side, taking his tally to six for the campaign already.

The 27-year-old is averaging almost a goal per game and has scored more than half of Liverpool 's Premier League goals this season.

Like last weekend at Brentford , Isak didn't necessarily set the game alight, but again it was another crucial goal from the Swede. His strike gave Liverpool breathing space against a Brighton team that had 64% possession and actually ended the game with a higher xG than Andoni Iraola's side.

In the end, Liverpool saw the game out and this was arguably their finest display in the league under Iraola, who secured his first league win at Anfield at the fourth time of asking .

Only Erling Haaland (nine) has scored more Premier League goals this season than Isak and when Liverpool signed him from Newcastle these were the numbers they expected.

During Isak's struggles in an injury-plagued campaign in 2025-26, the belief inside the club was that this was a long-term signing and any judgement would be reserved for when he was fully fit. Judging by recent performances, that patience is proving to be warranted.

"Today, the performance was really good against a really good team," Isak said.

"The first half is really what we want to be about - winning balls and the intensity."

The exciting thing for Iraola and Liverpool is that Isak is nowhere near his best yet, and that should be a cause of worry for the rest of the top flight. It is Arsenal next up in the league.

"Alex [Isak] is threatening, especially if we can get him in those positions and we can provide him good crosses. In this case, it's a matter of Bradley [Barcola] winning the duel and being faster than the opposition to get us in that position," said Iraola.

Isak, Barcola and Wirtz turn up - player ratings for Liverpool v Brighton

For Iraola, this was a fourth win in a row since the loss to Manchester City at Anfield a fortnight ago.

The fans who braved the conditions after Storm Boelo were treated to a display where Liverpool were aggressive from the outset and defended really well to keep a Brighton side that scored 15 league goals in their previous four games at bay.

Bar an early chance for Yasin Ayari, which the Swede blazed over, Fabian Hurzeler's side didn't have any major chances of note.

Ronald Araujo was again immense and the Liverpool backline kept their fourth clean sheet in eight league games this season.

Interestingly, Liverpool 's possession of 35.6% was their second lowest on record (since 2003-04) in a Premier League home win.

Iraola's Bournemouth side certainly preferred to have less of the ball and this was a reminder that, with the quality at his disposal going forward, Liverpool are perhaps fine with teams coming to Anfield and having more of the ball, especially if it means the opposition aren't set up in a low block .

Both Florian Wirtz and Barcola were excellent and Cody Gakpo threatened all afternoon too, with Wirtz unlucky not to be credited for the goal when his strike took a deflection off Pascal Gross and gave Liverpool the lead.

Slowly but surely, his confidence is increasing in a Liverpool shirt and it is clear to see the impact he has on a game.

The German just needs the numbers to improve on his end and Liverpool will hope that he isn’t set for a spell on the sidelines after he was substituted in the second half.

"Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle," said Iraola.

"It doesn't look very big but we are playing every three days so we need to see where he is."

As for Barcola, there is a style to his play that can energise a crowd and the way he won possession for Isak's goal felt like it ticked off exactly what Iraola wanted with the high press and sheer desire to win the ball back.

That left Isak to finish instinctively and Barcola imitated Isak's celebration, just like they did last weekend in west London, as Liverpool moved up to fourth.

Theirs is a combination that cost the Reds a total of £248m but if they can keep on combining and winning games, that will do just fine for Iraola and Liverpool .

articles.title: Hibernian: Does Grant Hanley's striker cameo pose questions?
articles.summary: Grant Hanley was called upon to be a makeshift striker for Hibs against Celtic, but what does it signal for the Scottish Premiership's bottom side?
articles.body:
With eight minutes to go at Easter Road on Sunday, Hibs needed a goal to salvage something from their Scottish Premiership match against Celtic.

Head coach Marink Reedijk turned to his bench in search of a spark and summoned old head Grant Hanley, tasking the grizzled centre-back with playing up front.

It was a damning indictment of the options available to Reedijk and also a sign of slight desperation after two defeats in his opening two matches in charge.

Hanley did have something of an impact during his short cameo. He won one header which led to a chance for Josh Mulligan and was close to getting on the end of a deflected effort from Rabbi Matondo.

Ultimately, if Hanley had scored or created a Hibs equaliser, Reedijk would have been hailed as a genius. As it was, they lost 2-1 and remain bottom of the Scottish Premiership.

"I saw that we struggled to get the momentum. Celtic tried to play the game out and I wanted to change something to get a little bit of chaos," Reedijk said when asked for his thinking behind the substitution.

"Eventually I think it worked, I think [Hanley] did a fantastic job because at the end of the day he was a handful for the two defenders and they didn't know what to do about him."

Celtic restore four-point lead with narrow win at Hibs

Former Hibs midfielder Scott Allan says the fact Reedijk felt a need to make the change is a concern.

"The biggest surprise was the impact Grant Hanley had up front," Allan said. "That would also be a concern if you're a Hibs fan because that's probably the impact they were looking for from Ante Suto.

"I thought there was a real lack of quality within the Hibs side throughout.

"I refuse to take a positive that Grant Hanley coming up front for the last 10 minutes and being a target man is something you want to be talking about.

"Hibs have to be better than that as your option to try and get back into a game. I understand certain times call for a bit of chaos, but that is not for me. They've got to be better than that."

Suto came on 15 minutes before Hanley and failed to have any sort of meaningful impact on the game.

Suto and Nathan Lowe are the two strikers in the Hibs squad suited to lead the line. Martin Boyle pulled out of the side on the morning of the game through illness, while goalscorer Owen Elding and record signing Thibault Klidje are different types of forwards.

The club's fanbase have expressed dissatisfaction with sporting director Malky Mackay and the recruitment made under his watch.

Until January, Reedijk is stuck with the tools at his disposal and given Hibs are bottom of the table, that is a massive worry.

Allan was asked if he has seen any improvements since Reedijk replaced former head coach David Gray.

"For me, no," he said. "Do they look like they're trying to change the style of play? We've heard a lot of talk about it, but I haven't really seen it. Moving forward, Hibs have to start winning games of football."

articles.title: Giráldez: "El punto es bueno y justo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico reconoce que el cansancio les pasó factura en el segundo tiempo
articles.summary: El técnico reconoce que el cansancio les pasó factura en el segundo tiempo
articles.body: De la justicia del marcador, del cansancio en el segundo tiempo, de las dos partes diferenciadas o de la cuarta portería a cero, habló Claudio Giráldez tras el empate ante el Betis. Cansancio: "Se ha visto una diferencia muy notoria entre la primera parte y la segunda, en todos los aspectos vinculados a la energía. Hemos tirado mucho balón, fruto del cansancio. Nos ha faltado un poco de piernas para aguantar en la presión, en la segunda parte nos ha costado muchísimo girar la pelota". Dos tiempos diferenciados: "La segunda parte no me ha gustado, hemos tenido amor propio y nos hemos agarrado a un bloque bajo bien trabajado en la mayoría de las situaciones del juego. El punto es bueno y justo. En la primera parte, la primera media hora representa la línea del partido del Celtic, que es lo que queremos ver del equipo. Ordenados en la presión, equilibrados, teniendo el balón y haciéndolo circular. Para nosotros era importante ponernos por delante por el esfuerzo del jueves ya que el partido se nos ha hecho un poco largo". Nivel del Betis: "Ellos son un equipazo, de un nivel altísimo. Nueve de nueve puntos en Champions y cuartos en LaLiga. Es una pena que estos partidos se jueguen con tanta fatiga en las piernas porque desmerecen el espectáculo que se podía presenciar con dos equipes tan bonitos de ver y tan alegres". Cuarta portería a cero: "Es un aspecto totalmente positivo. Hace que cuando te faltan un poco las fuerzas, puedes estar sobreviviendo. Son siete jornadas seguidas sin perder en Liga y habla de esa fiabilidad".

articles.title: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds: Regis Le Bris' side remain bottom of Premier League as goalless draw extends winless run
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Sunderland draw 0-0 with Leeds at the Stadium of Light; Brian Brobbey missed a big chance for the hosts; Dominic Calvert-Lewin's penalty claim was waved away; Sunderland remain bottom of the table, Leeds climb into seventh
articles.body:
Brian Brobbey, featuring for the first time since September 20, came closest to breaking the deadlock but had his effort quickly smothered by James Trafford after racing through on goal in the first half.

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin was a doubt heading into the fixture but started the game. A risk, by Daniel Farke's own admission, which almost paid off when he went down in the area but claims for a penalty were quickly waved away.

VAR checked and cleared the incident and decided Robin Roefs got a hand to the ball, despite the Leeds forward getting to the ball first.

Former Newcastle midfielder Sean Longstaff, who was greeted by boos at the Stadium of Light, was twice denied in the latter stages after Roefs tipped one shot wide and the other was blocked on the line.

The draw means Regis Le Bris' side remain bottom of the table, while a point takes Leeds up into seventh.

Weather warnings were in place across northern parts of England and Scotland over the weekend for Storm Boelo, including Sunderland which had an amber warning for wind until 9pm on Sunday night.

Given the poor weather conditions, Sunderland posted a statement on social media just over four hours before kick-off confirming the game would be going ahead, with the club advising supporters to "take extra care" on their way to the ground.

A windswept Daniel Farke was pictured among the arrivals at the ground as powerful gusts swirled around Wearside and on the pitch during the match.

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris speaking to Sky Sports:

"It's a positive [point], the more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.

"It's still a long journey, we know with this busy schedule playing in Europe, playing in the Carabao Cup, it's a new challenge for us and we need to embrace it.

"I think we showed this afternoon that we are in this challenge, we want to embrace it and be ourselves and we probably deserved a bit more today."

Sunderland defender Luke O'Nien speaking to Sky Sports:

"I think the wind played a big part and credit to both defences and the attacks as well to be able to keep it to no goals in that swirling wind.

"I think it was a good effort from everybody so obviously we want three points from where we are in the table but keep putting up the performances like that and we'll get some.

"I think the table always reflects fairly where teams deserve to be, and I think over the course of the season, if we keep putting in performances like that, it will represent where we should be.

"But the table always reflects where people should be but we need to keep looking at ourselves, don't look at other anyone else, it's no one else's fault but us and we know that."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Will Michael Carrick be sacked? Man United manager says he doesn’t know
articles.summary: Manchester United’s 0-3 home loss to Bournemouth has left the 20-time champions winless in eight Premier League games.
articles.body:
Amid increasing pressure on his team and a growing threat to his own position as manager, Michael Carrick says he will do what is best for Manchester United after a 3-0 demolition by Bournemouth plunged his future into doubt.

Winless in eight games in all competitions, the 20-time English champions slipped to within one point of the relegation zone after a damaging defeat at Old Trafford on Sunday.

“It’s a tough situation,” Carrick told British broadcaster Sky Sports. “What is next? I don’t know.

“I’ll always do what’s best for this football club. I’ve said it all along; I don’t change that now. I love what I do. I love the responsibility, but we’ll have to wait and see.”

Asked in a post-match news conference if he expects to be sacked in the coming days, Carrick replied: “I totally understand the situation. I’m not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place.”

Despite a dismal run of results, the United fans largely supported the former midfielder as he made his way off the field at full-time before they turned on the club’s players.

“I have mixed emotions to have that connection with the supporters in the moment we’re in. I need time to digest that,” added Carrick.

“I appreciate their support but the situation is where it’s at. We haven’t been good enough.”

Carrick’s decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench and not even introduce the Portuguese international as a substitute backfired.

Fernandes, last season’s Premier League player of the year, had criticised Carrick’s tactics after the 4-1 thrashing by Como on Wednesday.

Carrick said before the game that his call was a “pure football” decision, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match.

“There’s always times in games when you are trying to change the course of the game and to make a difference,” said Carrick as he swerved questions on Fernandes’s absence. “Those were the decisions we made today.”

Carrick was appointed on a two-year deal only in May after a successful caretaker spell in charge led United to third place in the Premier League last season.

However, he has been unable to arrest the club’s steep decline since his former boss Alex Ferguson retired as manager in 2013.

United were outspent by many of their rivals in the transfer market as they added just three midfielders – Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.

But Carrick said a lack of investment did not justify such a decline in results.

“Last season to finish third was a really good achievement in the circumstances,” added Carrick.

“We understood where that left us, what was next, what needed to be done and how we needed to improve, and where we were at as a team and as a group at that stage.

“I definitely knew that we hadn’t cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn’t mean to say that it should have gone this way.”

articles.title: When is the 2026 Ballon d’Or, who are the favourites, and how can you watch it?
articles.summary: Al Jazeera Sport breaks down the award-voting criteria, top candidates and history ahead of the ceremony in London.
articles.body:
The Ballon d’Or, football’s most prestigious individual honour, will be awarded on Monday, with Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe among the frontrunners in the men’s category and Spain’s Alexia Putellas the favourite to pick the women’s award for the third time.

Given to the best player of the 2025-26 season, the upcoming ceremony will mark the award’s 70th edition, and the first time it is held outside France.

Ahead of Monday’s official gala, here’s everything to know about the award, its history and more:

The Ballon d’Or is the highest individual award given to a footballer, based on his or her performance in the previous season.

The award was created in 1956 by two sports writers, Gabriel Hanot and Jacques Ferran, from France Football, a French magazine.

Originally, the men’s award was limited to European players, but in 1995 it was expanded to include all players of any origin active at European clubs. Finally, in 2007, it became a global award with all professional footballers being eligible.

The women’s Ballon d’Or started in 2018 when Ada Hegerberg was named the inaugural winner.

The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) and Groupe Amaury – owners of France Football and L’Equipe – have co-organised the Ballon d’Or since the 2024 edition.

The winner is chosen by an international jury of specialised journalists, with one representative per country: the top 100 nations according to the FIFA rankings for the men’s award, and the top 50 for the women’s award.

The FIFA ranking used is the one in effect at the time the nominee lists were published, which in this case was on September 8, 2026.

Each jury member selects 10 players in descending order of merit from a 30-player shortlist.

The list is then compiled by the editorial staff of France Football, members of L’Equipe’s editorial team, at least one member of the previous edition’s jury, and UEFA ambassadors Luis Figo and Fabio Capello for the men’s trophy, and Nadine Kessler for the women’s trophy.

The 10 selected players receive 15, 12, 10, 8, 7, 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 point respectively, based on the order of their rankings in the voting.

In the end, the Ballon d’Or is awarded to the player with the highest overall score.

Players are judged for their performances over the whole of last season. For this year’s award, the timeline is from August 3, 2025, until July 19, 2026.

Jurors are asked to take three factors into consideration when ranking players. The Ballon d’Or regulations list the following in order of importance:

Individual performances, decisive and impressive character

In the men’s category , England’s captain Kane, who scored an incredible 73 goals last season, is the bookmakers’ favourite to win the Ballon d’Or. As of Sunday, he holds about 70 percent of the market share.

Kane was the Bundesliga’s top scorer for the third year running and also earned a second European Golden Shoe. The 33-year-old won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich, and led England to a third-place finish at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Frenchman Mbappe, who won the Golden Boot at the World Cup and set an all-time goals record, is the second favourite, followed by teenage winger Lamine Yamal, who was part of Spain’s world title-winning squad.

The men’s 30-player star-studded shortlist also features Argentina’s 2022 World Cup winner Lionel Messi and the last two Ballon d’Or recipients, Ousmane Dembele and Rodri.

For the women’s Ballon d’Or, Spain captain Alexia Putellas is the frontrunner after leading her previous club Barcelona to quadruple glory, which included the Liga F and Women’s Champions League crowns.

Putellas, who won the Ballon d’Or in 2021 and 2022, is hoping to match teammate and reigning winner Aitana Bonmati’s record of three trophies.

Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw, the Women’s Super League top scorer for a third campaign in a row, Barca’s Ewa Pajor, the women’s UCL top scorer, and Lyon’s Melchie Dumornay, who won a domestic treble, are also in the running.

Where and when is the Ballon d’Or ceremony?

The 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony will be held at the London Palladium on Monday, October 26, marking the first time it is being held in Britain.

Organisers said the decision to move the ceremony away from France, its usual host country, was made to pay tribute to the 1956 inaugural Ballon d’Or winner, England’s Stanley Matthews.

The red carpet will begin at 18:00 GMT and last for about an hour and a half.

It will be followed by the official ceremony at 20:00 GMT. France and Arsenal striker Thierry Henry and sports journalist Kate Scott will be the cohosts.

US rapper French Montana and English singer Jorja Smith will perform at the gala.

Where can I watch the ceremony and follow it online?

Al Jazeera Sport will have live coverage of the awards ceremony from 17:00 GMT.

DAZN will livestream the ceremony for free in most countries. Also, viewers in France can watch the ceremony on L’Equipe TV, while Telefonica will televise it in Spain.

Who has won the most Ballon d’Or awards?

Argentine legend Lionel Messi has a record eight Ballon d’Or awards in his trophy cabinet. He also holds the record for the most consecutive wins (four), taking the trophy home in 2009-2012.

His longtime rival, Cristiano Ronaldo, is second on the list, with five Ballon d’Ors.

France and Paris Saint-Germain forward Dembele won the 2025 Ballon d’Or, while Spain’s captain Rodri was the 2024 winner.

Which other awards are given at the Ballon d’Or?

A total of 13 awards will be presented on Monday, including the men’s and women’s Ballon d’Ors.

Men’s and women’s Kopa Trophy (for U-21 players)

Men’s and women’s Yashin Trophy (for best goalkeeper)

Men’s and women’s Gerd Muller Trophy (for best striker)

Men’s and women’s Johan Cruyff Trophy (for best coach)

Socrates Award (for humanitarian work, charity projects, and social solidarity initiatives)

articles.title: Pierre Sage: Pressure grows as fans turn on Palace boss
articles.summary: Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage had a tough act to follow in Oliver Glasner - and four months into the job the Frenchman is already under big pressure.
articles.body:
"Oliver Glasner achieved some amazing things, and now I have to do the same," Pierre Sage said after replacing the man who delivered an FA Cup, a European trophy and Community Shield during two years in charge at Selhurst Park.

Four months into a three-year contract, the Frenchman is already under big pressure after a fifth defeat in eight Premier League games left the Eagles in the bottom four.

Palace have failed to win their past four games and Sunday's 2-0 home defeat by Newcastle was greeted with boos from home fans, who had turned up hoping to see a positive response after last weekend's 5-0 humiliation at fierce rivals Brighton .

"There is no noise inside the club," said Sage when asked about his future in his post-match media conference.

"The boos are normal because we don't have the result.

"The noise is the consequence of the result of the team, and at the moment we don't have what we expect.

"Inside, we are just really focused on solutions. How to be better, how to create the conditions to compete, and we will continue our work, and there's no noise inside."

Asked about boos from home fans during the match and at full-time, Sage accepted it was an expected response after failing to win.

"It's normal that people lose patience when you lose, because everybody wants to win. Today it was not the case."

Sage was named Ligue 1 manager of the year after leading Lens to a second-place finish as well as a French Cup triumph.

But could time already be running out for the 47-year-old?

Sage struck a defiant tone during his post-match media conference as he addressed questions about his future for 20 minutes.

"I don't have to convince the people around the club. I just have to convince the players to do their best to compete and to continue to improve," he added when asked further about his job.

"After that, this kind of decision is for the chairman, to the owners, this kind of person.

"For me, the noise around the team, the noise around the club, it's only noise."

Palace have just seven points from their first eight league games in the post-Glasner era.

After losing to Everton and Manchester City in their first two matches, Palace won at Fulham before losing at home to newly promoted Ipswich .

They secured a rare clean sheet in a goalless draw at Leeds before coming from behind to beat Nottingham Forest at Selhurst Park on 11 October.

They have since lost at his former club Lyon in the Europa League, and Brighton , before drawing 2-2 against Besiktas in Istanbul on Thursday.

However, patience is clearly wearing thin after fans reacted to the latest defeat by Newcastle .

In addition, Palace have the worst defensive record in the Premier League after conceding 19 goals in eight games.

Their next Premier League match is at improving Tottenham next Saturday, before hosting Liverpool on 8 November going into the international break.

Palace's first game back is at fellow strugglers Coventry City on 21 November.

French football expert Julien Laurens said Sage needed to be more ruthless.

"He's a lovely guy. He's maybe a little bit too nice at times," Laurens, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, added.

"Remember when Crystal Palace beat Fulham earlier in the season? That was Palace's first win of the season and he felt sorry for Fulham .

"You don't feel sorry in this league. This Premier League is ruthless. It's the top, top level. This is the best league in the world.

"You can't feel sorry for the opposition you have just beaten, especially when this is your first win and you needed it badly.

"But this is the kind of guy that he is."

Sage's Lens side were built on aggressive pressing and a willingness to attack quickly once they won the ball back.

The Opta numbers showed a team intent on regaining possession high up the pitch.

Lens made 426 high turnovers during the 2025-26 season, frequently turning those moments into chances - producing 69 shots and seven goals.

However, Palace are clearly struggling to fire under Sage's leadership.

"He needs to do things slightly differently," added Laurens. "There is pressure everywhere in the Premier League."

Former Manchester United and England forward Dion Dublin said Sage needed to be tougher if he is to have a long-term future at Palace.

"It's no good being lovely with everything," added Dublin, also speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live.

"Things can't be lovely when you are a Premier League manager. You will just lose games and get sacked."

Former Leeds United forward Lucy Ward told 5 Live: "He has proved himself at Lyon and Lens. Being a little bit too nice doesn't help."

articles.title: Gary Neville slams Man Utd players for downing tools and turning on Michael Carrick after Bournemouth defeat
articles.summary: Gary Neville on Man Utd's players: "A few of them aren't that professional. There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should."
articles.body:
The embarrassing defeat at Old Trafford extended Manchester United's winless run to eight games in all competitions, leaving Michael Carrick's future as head coach in serious doubt .

Neville fears Carrick is facing the sack and, speaking on his podcast, the Sky Sports pundit turned his ire towards the club's under-performing players, accusing them of a lack of professionalism.

"It was a shocker today, a nothing of a performance," he said.

"Nothing against Tottenham here, nothing against Como, nothing against Atletico Madrid. A little bit against Leeds, it was a bit of a fight, but nothing against Fulham. That was a waste of time.

"So, this is a pattern of nothings, of players switching off and downing tools."

Bruno Fernandes was an unused substitute after his public criticism of Carrick's tactics against Como, while Lisandro Martinez, who spoke out against the club's hierarchy after the Atletico Madrid game, only featured as a second-half substitute.

"Michael Carrick is a brilliant man," added Neville.

"He's a man of integrity, of credibility, of decency, of professionalism, of high-quality football and consistency and reliability. Everything the group of players in that dressing room aren't.

"And he's going to suffer for it because he's not been able to deliver. It's been too much for him in these last few months.

"He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him.

"I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes.

"If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.

"A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them.

"There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should.

"Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players."

Neville hopes Carrick doesn't bear the full brunt of United's recent struggles and fears they could go another decade without a Premier League title unless there are changes at the top of the club.

"It's 14 years now without a Premier League title," he said.

"That will be another five or 10 before you know it because there are other clubs set up for success and Manchester United aren't.

"They are making poor decisions. From a business perspective, this is really damaging.

"It can't just be the manager again. There has got to be consequences above that. You can't keep letting the people pick the manager who keep getting it wrong."

articles.title: CFP Playoff Bracket, Scenarios and Bowl Projections After 2026-27 Week 9 AP Rankings
articles.summary: The hierarchy of College Football Playoff contenders switched up once again after Week 8 due to the losses suffered by the BYU Cougars and Texas Tech Red Raiders.
articles.body:
The hierarchy of College Football Playoff contenders switched up once again after Week 8 due to the losses suffered by the BYU Cougars and Texas Tech Red Raiders.

BYU dropped six spots from No. 2 to No. 8 in Sunday's AP Top 25 . Texas Tech experienced a similar stumble from No. 8 to No. 13.

Saturday's results in the Big 12 allowed the Utah Utes, who beat the Houston Cougars at home, to move up to No. 6.

Utah is one of three unbeaten teams left in the FBS alongside the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes and the No. 7 UCLA Bruins.

UCLA is one of a few unexpected teams inside the top 10. The Kentucky Wildcats also fit into that category at No. 9. Kentucky, the Georgia Bulldogs and Alabama Crimson Tide are the only three SEC teams inside the top 10 going into Week 9.

Utah Up to No. 6, BYU Down to No. 8 In Big 12 Reshuffling

The Big 12 entered Week 8 with three teams in the top 10.

Utah's win combined with the losses suffered by BYU and Texas Tech caused a reshuffling in the Week 9 AP poll.

Utah is now the top team in the Big 12 at No. 6. The Utes have a potentially tricky three-game stretch ahead of them now. They go on the road next week to face the Cincinnati Bearcats, who upset Texas Tech in Week 8, before a November 7 rivalry battle with BYU.

A road trip to Arizona on November 14 is also on the schedule. That could be a tough test one game after the rivalry game.

The best-case scenario in the Big 12 is for Utah, BYU and Texas Tech to all finish the regular season with one loss. That would mean BYU beats Utah on November 7.

BYU's margin for error is smaller now because of its loss to the UCF Knights. The Cougars' only remaining ranked opponent is Utah.

As for Texas Tech, it gets Arizona at home next week and then faces a tough test on the road at the Oklahoma State Cowboys.

With all the carnage happening in the SEC, the Big Ten only having a few elite teams and the ACC in a weak state, the Big 12 is in position to have three playoff teams, even with all of the chaos that occurred on Saturday.

Texas Leaps Up to No. 11 After Win Over Ole Miss

The Texas Longhorns surged back up to No. 11 following its win over the Ole Miss Rebels and the chaos that occurred elsewhere.

Arch Manning and Co. moved up eight positions in the poll to No. 11, which would be good enough to be an at-large team in the 12-team CFB Playoff field if the season ended today.

Texas has a weird resume, though, with three top-15 wins and two losses to unranked teams.

The Longhorns, with their two losses, still have a small margin for error to make the playoff field. They visit the Missouri Tigers and LSU Tigers in the first two weeks of November.

If Texas wins out, it will absolutely be in the playoff, but if it suffers another defeat, it'll sit in a tough spot to qualify as an at-large team.

UCLA is one of the unexpected programs inside the top 10.

The Bruins moved to 7-0 on Saturday. They are now up to No. 7 in the AP poll.

UCLA has a very realistic path to the playoff as well. It doesn't have a single ranked opponent left on its schedule after the USC Trojans dropped out of the poll.

The Bruins do have two difficult road trips left against the Minnesota Golden Gophers and Michigan Wolverines, but they could be favored in both of those contests.

If UCLA survives those trips, it could be undefeated to end the regular season, which would guarantee its spot in the playoff field.

Even a one-loss UCLA should get into the field given how many teams have one or two losses at this juncture of the season.

articles.title: Goleada de líder
articles.standfirst: El Castellón gana al Sporting y da un golpe en la clasificación
articles.summary: Maty Orozco dio tres asistencias para que Jakobsen (2 goles) y Suero marcasen
articles.body: El Castellón ha dado otra muestra de poderío al imponerse por 4-0 al Sporting para asaltar el lidetaro en solitario en un partido encarrilado en el primer tiempo con los goles de Jakobsen y Suero y sentenciado en la reanudación con el doblete del danés y el tanto de Álvaro García. El equipo de Pablo Hernández abrió el marcador muy pronto a través de Jakobsen, que aprovechó una pared con Maty Orozco para plantarse solo ante Yáñez y batirle en el mano a mano. El Sporting reaccionó y encerró a continuación al Castellón en una fase en la que tuvo dos ocasiones por medio de Gaspar que desbarató Matthys con sendos paradones (13, y 25'). Y justo después de la segunda opción visitante, el Castellón puso el 2-0 en otra acción combinativa resuelta por Suero con asistencia de Maty. El centrocampista madrileño disparó desde la frontal para ampliar la ventaja castellonense. Suero pudo hacer el tercero cerca del descanso con un zurdazo al larguero. El segundo tiempo, de dominio local, empezó con una ocasión clara de Suero con solo medio minuto jugado tras un error rojiblanco en la salida de balón. Pero no perdonó en el 52 Jakobsen aprovechando otra pared con Maty Orozco para sentenciar con el 3-0. El danés tuvo la opción del triplete a continuación, pero se lo impidió Yáñez. No perdonó Álvaro García a tres minutos del final con un disparo desde la frontal que no pudo detener el meta visitante. El Castellón suma de esta forma su segunda victoria consecutiva para liderar la clasificación y empezar a marcar diferencias en la zona de ascenso. El danés Jakobsen ha demostrado su capacidad para ejercer de delantero centro ante la baja de Camara marcando dos goles frente al Sporting y gozando de ocasiones para hacer el triplete. El escandinavo suma tres tantos esta temporada.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or: Lyon and Scotland's Caroline Weir would swap nominations for World Cup
articles.summary: Caroline Weir reflects on her Ballon d'Or nomination while eyeing a World Cup spot with Scotland.
articles.body:
When a football pitch is in sight, there are few things Caroline Weir cannot do well.

But, leaning against a stand at St Mirren Park in her Scotland training gear, the back-to-back Ballon d'Or nominee struggles and squirms when she is forced to talk about herself.

The 31-year-old has again been named on the 30-player shortlist after an exceptional year for club and country - having swapped Real Madrid for eight-time European champions Lyon and been named Scotland captain - but she is not one for shouting about her achievements.

"Yeah, it's cool, I guess," said Weir, who has scored 11 international goals - including three hat-tricks - in a year she signed-off as the Galactica's all-time goalscorer.

"It's always cool to be included in a list where there are so many good players on it - that's a real honour but it's very subjective."

Downplaying the feat with the same ease she glides by defenders, Weir is much more at home discussing her determination and "desperation" of reaching the World Cup in Brazil next summer.

She says "it all means nothing if we don't achieve our goal of going to the World Cup".

Attention will swiftly shift back to that goal after the ceremony in London on Monday, with Sweden standing in the way of Scotland's major tournament return.

But for one night, the light will shine on the magical midfielder, whether she likes it or not.

'Possessed' Davidson fills Weir gap as Scots set up glamour Sweden tie

Scotland beat Czechs to set up World Cup play-off with Sweden

It will not be first time she's been under the spotlight - and likely not the last.

Her outrageous ability and frequency of hauling Scotland over the line means Weir often writes the headlines herself.

She did not feature in the Scots' second leg against the Czech Republic in their World Cup qualifying round one play-off after pulling up injured in the warm-up, but she still dominated the back pages, such is her importance and influence.

Before that injury, which she has yet to return from, she did not have plans to walk the red carpet at the Palladium with a Champions League match at home to Inter Milan on Wednesday - but who knows if she will be able to now.

At last year's event in Paris - after checking "the list was legit" - she went all-out with her husband Josh in Paris and immersed herself in the "unbelievable" night.

"There were just superstars everywhere you looked," she recalled.

"We got on the plane from Madrid and Figo was sat right in front of us. That's how it started and how it went on.

"We were just loving every minute and we were so happy to be there."

All you need to know about the 2026 Ballon d'Or

A Ballon d'Or campaign as fierce off the pitch as on it

Her first nomination holds a special place, especially as she was the first Scottish woman to receive one - in the same year Scott McTominay did too - and in her comeback year from an ACL injury.

This year, though, it's been down to others to make a big deal of the recognition.

In the recent international camp, team-mates and close pals Erin Cuthbert and Claire Emslie presented her with a commemorative shirt , external in honour of her incredible accomplishments.

Both showered her with compliments but Weir could not be quicker in returning the praise to her best pal Emslie, who recently scored her first goal since becoming a mum, with Weir calling her "an inspiration". Takes one to know one.

As soon as the discussion shifts from the glitz and glamour of the Ballon d'Or, the Scotland skipper can re-emerge from her shell.

Despite both being the other side of 30, she and the "unbelievable multi-tasker" Emslie, who have been friends for 20 years, fall back into their old ways.

"When we're back together, we haven't grown up that much considering we're 31 and 32," Weir said.

"She's still my best friend, we're having a laugh and then she goes into mum mode, which is the most incredible thing to watch, and I'm just in awe, it's so special."

The pair are two of six current Scots who were part of the history-making squad at the 2019 World Cup, which arguably fuels their fire even more to return.

Since the heartbreak in Helsinki nearly two years ago when Pedro Martinez Losa's side failed to qualify for Euro 2025, Weir has never hidden her desire to make Brazil 2027.

In fact, she does not do many interviews without mentioning it.

In March, she admitted she was "borderline desperate" . In April, it was a case of "I want nothing more this year than to qualify". In June, she said " I'm doing everything and anything to realise my dream". You get the gist.

Such comments were all made before it was confirmed back-to-back World Cup semi-finalist Sweden are in Scotland's way.

But it will take a lot more than that iconic yellow shirt to shift Weir's focus.

"It's my biggest objective," Weir said. "It's the most important thing for me.

"I want to be at a World Cup, I want Scotland to be at a World Cup.

"I'd swap everything, nominations, goals, for this team to get to a World Cup and that's all I can really think about."

articles.title: Man Utd 1-1 Man City: Andree Jeglertz's City drop behind Chelsea on goal difference as perfect start ends in derby
articles.summary: Match report and free match highlights as Man Utd draw 1-1 with Man City; Elisabeth Terland's late equaliser means City's perfect start to WSL season ends; Khadija Shaw had given visitors the lead, who now fall behind Chelsea on goal difference
articles.body:
City looked set for victory as Khadija Shaw finally broke the deadlock with a little over 20 minutes to go. However, it was Shaw who inadvertently set up Terland for the equaliser in the last minute of normal time.

Both teams came into the contest in good spirits. City had made a perfect start in their opening six WSL games, while United had been starting to click under Eva Olid.

It was the hosts who appeared more likely to find the opener following a tense first half. They were on top after the break, with Jess Park ratting the crossbar on the hour mark as they looked to make their dominance count.

Shaw had been having an uncharacteristically quiet evening, being heckled by home fans and marked out of the game by Maya Le Tissier in the first 45. She targeted Dominique Janssen when the game resumed and the switch paid off.

The PFA Player of the Year backed into the Dutch defender before turning and firing through her legs to find the bottom corner and give City the lead against the run of play on her 100th WSL appearance.

It was a bitter blow for the Red Devils, whose hard work looked set to be unrewarded. That was until Shaw's tame clearance from a deep Le Tissier cross fell to the feet of Terland, who dispatched perfectly to snatch a share of the spoils.

The result means that City only go level on points with Chelsea at the top, but fall behind Sonia Bompastor's side on goal difference following their come-from-behind win against Crystal Palace .

89: GOAL! Terland nets dramatic late equaliser.

Jeglertz: Disappointed to concede so late

Man City boss Andree Jeglertz speaking with Sky Sports :

"You remember the last five minutes where you concede a goal and you feel disappointed.

"Overall, it's a fantastic football game. An intense game, a lot of emotions during the whole game. United is giving us a big fight. You can't say anything about the result but of course you are disappointing when you concede late and had a big chance before that.

"I'm so happy for her [Bunny Shaw]. A tough game for her. A lot of hits and knocks and then she's the one scoring for us. She has done it so many times. At the same time, we always want to win games."

Manchester United striker Elisabeth Terland speaking with Sky Sports :

"I think with the way the game evolves we should be happy with a point. I'm really happy with the performance today. We could've come away with a win. We will take the point at the end of the day.

"We had the chances today to get the goals. Even in the first half, we should be up. There's a lot to take from this game and this is the standard going forward.

"It's a fun way to play football. If we can play like this every week, it is enjoyable. We are competing against a top team and should probably win. That just speaks for itself."

articles.title: Óskarsson, en una racha que podría ser mejor
articles.standfirst: El delantero islandés marcó ante el Levante por tercer encuentro seguido, pero tuvo ocasiones como para haber logrado más tantos
articles.summary: El delantero islandés marcó ante el Levante por tercer encuentro seguido, pero tuvo ocasiones como para haber logrado más tantos
articles.body: Orri Óskarsson marcó contra el Levante por tercer encuentro consecutivo, una racha que le permitió colocarse con cuatro goles como el segundo máximo realizador de la Real Sociedad en lo que llevamos de temporada, por detrás de Luka Sucic que lleva cinco. El delantero islandés podría haber pasado al croata de haber estado más efectivo, ya que dispuso de otras tres o cuatro muy buenas opciones para ampliar su cuenta y el marcador en favor de su equipo. Óskarsson, que ya terminó la pasada campaña en una buena racha, con cuatro dianas en los últimos cinco encuentros que disputó, la continuó en la pretemporada, con tres tantos en los amistosos jugados, y no tuvo que esperar más que a la tercera jornada liguera para estrenarse en este curso, pero luego vio frenada su gran trayectoria al enlazar cinco citas sin marcar. El ariete de Reikiavik está alternando la titularidad con la suplencia, en función de si la Real juega más al ataque o no tanto, y después de tres partidos sentado en el banquillo, aprovechó su vuelta al once en Málaga para reencontrarse con el gol, siendo el inicio de esta buena racha en la que está, al ver luego portería en Lillestrom y volver a hacerlo ante el Levante. Óskarsson se coloca con cuatro goles en esta campaña, tres en LaLiga y uno en la Europa League, pero podía llevar algunos más, porque ha dispuesto de unas cuantas ocasiones claras para ello, sin ir más lejos frente al conjunto granota, al que chutó en posición clara al menos tres veces más en la primera parte y otra en la segunda, aunque sin puntería. Lo bueno para la Real es que está viendo portería con asiduidad y no está teniendo los problemas físicos de las temporadas anteriores, por lo que es una opción muy buena para Matarazzo de cara a poder jugar con alguien por delante de Oyarzabal o, al menos, tenerle como opción en el banquillo cuando decides que el capitán sea el futbolista más adelantado.

articles.title: Can Carrick survive Man United’s slump and Fernandes fallout?
articles.summary: Manchester United cheer Michael Carrick off after Bournemouth loss but boo Bruno Fernandes, what now for crisis club?
articles.body:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick left the Old Trafford pitch on Sunday to the sound of his name being sung by the adoring home support, but he may never lead the team onto the field again.

His players followed him and the message delivered to them and the club captain Bruno Fernandes, who was an unused substitute, was quite different.

The 3-0 thumping by Bournemouth was a result that marked a 40-year low for the crisis club and plunged it to new depths – and the fans were determined to let United’s owners and playing staff know it.

The opening seven league matches marked United’s worst start since 1986. The latest defeat, their sixth of the season, leaves the club just a point above the relegation zone and without a win in eight matches in all competitions.

What has happened between Fernandes and Carrick?

Fernandes, the Professional Footballers’ Association’s Player of the Year last season, was left among the substitutes on Sunday as a result of criticising Carrick after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation at Como in the UEFA Champions League.

The Portuguese player has been the Red Devils’ darling since he arrived in 2020, and seemed to have sealed his place as a club legend in a time of darkness with his accolade achieved on the back of United’s third-place finish, which they have only twice bettered in 13 years.

The award came as a result of his record number of assists in a Premier League season – all the more impressive in a side that lacked a spark anywhere else on the pitch.

The upturn in fortunes under Carrick’s interim position last term, when he replaced Ruben Amorim in January, resulted in his full-time appointment in the summer.

A tenure that may now have run its course, with him and United’s best player seemingly at loggerheads.

How have fans reacted to the Premier League giant’s fall?

The United fans are famously loyal to their managers and players. Boos for anyone associated with the home side at Old Trafford were relatively unheard of until the last two seasons.

Now the boss receiving the adulation on exiting one of world football’s greatest stages – the Theatre of Dreams – may be the one on whom the curtain is being pulled.

Fernandes is no villain in this piece, but United’s fans have delivered a clear message directly to the heart of the dressing room – sending it via the player who could do no wrong in the eyes of the supporters will leave the ears of every member of the squad ringing.

Outplayed is one thing, but being outrun and outfought is another.

What is the context of Man United’s demise?

United’s history has been one of rebuilds and comebacks. They have known difficult days – their most successful manager Sir Alex Ferguson was on the verge of the sack in 1990 before winning the FA Cup and beginning one of the greatest runs of trophy-laden eras in football.

Their wait for a league title stretched from 1967 – and the Holy Trinity of George Best, Bobby Charlton and Denis Law – to 1993, when Ferguson’s inspired signing of Eric Cantona ignited glory days even the biggest club in the world at the time had never seen.

Now, United are on the edge of a precipice – quite literally if the gap to the drop zone is even to be realistically contemplated. Perhaps United’s cross-town rivals City won’t be the only Manchester club facing relegation this season.

That is demise no one is truly considering yet.

Is it a case of Carrick or Fernandes for Man United?

They are, however, at a crossroads – and the divide between Carrick and Fernandes – his captain, who criticised the tactics that stopped United pressing their Italian opponents in midweek, is likely to see the axe fall on the manager rather than a valuable asset.

“Manchester United need to make the change tonight (Sunday),” former England team-mate of Carrick, Jamie Carragher, told British broadcaster Sky Sports when asked if a sacking was needed.

“The fans have taken the side of the manager, which is not about him being the manager, it’s about him being a huge figure in United’s history – and those players have done nothing compared to teams of the past.

“So Carrick is always going to win that fight – and rightly so – with Fernandes, no matter how talented a player he is.

“But also United – one of the biggest clubs in the world – are 16th in the table right now and that can’t happen – it can’t continue and Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties.

“He wants to be sacked. It’s become untenable. He doesn’t want to be sat in the dugout with those players.

“Imagine going into training with Fernandes after not bringing him on? It’s a rancid dressing room. He wants to be put out of his misery.”

Gary Neville, former Manchester United defender and team-mate of Carrick’s for club and country, added: “Carrick is popular, but the owners, the sporting department and the players are not.

“They will probably make a decision that will disgust United fans, but it is probably necessary.

What has Carrick said amid rumours of the sack?

The final word of the day belongs to the man in the middle of a power battle that has seen him win the popular vote, but one that is unlikely to sway the United hierarchy.

“I take the responsibility,” Carrick said in the post-match news conference. “I totally understand the situation, I’m not expecting anything, I’m carrying on as normal and I love this place.”

In something of a reference to dropping the club captain and the response he received from the crowd at the end, Carrick continued: “I always do what I feel is going to be the best for the club, whatever decision is made.

“I’ve tried to do everything I can to not be in this position and for a number of reasons, whatever they are, we’ve not been able to stop that happening to the position we’re in.

“I’ve always felt that support and always felt that connection with the [fans].

“I have to say it is mixed emotions, I didn’t really expect that from the supporters. The respect that I have for them and for them to show that back meant an awful lot.”

Emotions are running high at Old Trafford and, even though Carrick denied it, his fanfare at the end may well prove to have been his farewell.

The Theatre of Dreams has become a house of horrors – for the 11th manager since Ferguson retired and with United’s last Premier League title now stretching back to 2013.

articles.title: ‘A new direction is necessary’: Oregon fires a coach after another loss
articles.summary: The Oregon Ducks entered the 2026 season with College Football Playoff expectations, but their offense has fallen apart over the last few weeks. Now, head co...
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks entered the 2026 season with College Football Playoff expectations, but their offense has fallen apart over the last few weeks. Now, head coach Dan Lanning has decided that a change is needed.

On Sunday, Oregon announced that it had parted ways with one of its coaches on the offensive side of the ball, firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer, one day after a 21-10 loss to Illinois dropped the Ducks to 4-3.

Lanning said that a "new direction" was necessary to get the offense back on track.

Oregon hasn't scored more than 17 points in any of its last three games, and Saturday's loss in Champaign dropped the Ducks to 2-2 in Big Ten play.

Injuries have played a big part. Starting quarterback Dante Moore has been out since suffering a concussion against USC in Week 4, and Oregon has also dealt with injuries and absences at wide receiver.

In Moore's absence, Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas have struggled to move the ball. Raiola has completed 74 of 114 passes for 761 yards, six touchdowns, and two interceptions this season, while Thomas is 23-of-40 for 226 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

With Northwestern coming to Eugene next week, followed by a trip to Ohio State, Oregon's playoff hopes are hanging by a thread if they're not already dead.

On3's Pete Nakos was first to report that Oregon was moving on from Mehringer, and the school confirmed the news shortly after.

"Drew has been a valued member of this staff since 2022, and I am appreciative of everything he's done for Oregon," Lanning said in a statement . "He played a tremendous role in what this program has accomplished over the last several seasons.

"This was a decision I felt was in the best interest of our football program, as I believe a new direction is necessary to move our offense forward. I thank Drew for his efforts and wish him all the best."

Mehringer joined Oregon's staff as tight ends coach in 2022 and added co-offensive coordinator duties before the 2025 season. He took over as the full-time offensive coordinator this year after Will Stein left to become the head coach at Kentucky.

Oregon did not immediately announce who will take over as offensive coordinator or play-calling duties.

articles.title: Cuándo se entrega el Balón de Oro 2026: fecha, horario, lugar y dónde ver en TV la gala al mejor jugador del mundo
articles.standfirst: La ceremonia tendrá lugar en Londres
articles.summary: La ceremonia tendrá lugar en Londres
articles.body: El mundo del fútbol dirige sus focos hacia la capital británica para acoger una de las citas más esperadas del calendario anual, la ceremonia de entrega del Balón de Oro 2026. Con el 70.° aniversario de la prestigiosa galardón como telón de fondo, el evento se traslada por primera vez en su historia fuera de territorio francés para celebrarse en el emblemático London Palladium Theatre, en un claro homenaje a Sir Stanley Matthews. La máxima expectación recae sobre la pugna por suceder en el palmarés a Ousmane Dembélé y Aitana Bonmatí, con un abanico de estrellas consagradas y jóvenes talentos emergentes que aspiran a la gloria individual. Figuras como Lamine Yamal, Harry Kane y Kylian Mbappé acaparan la atención de los pronósticos en una edición especialmente abierta y reñida. La gala de entrega del Balón de Oro 2026 se celebrará el próximo lunes 26 de octubre a partir de las 21:00 horas (horario peninsular español). La ceremonia se podrá seguir en directo por televisión e internet en España a través de la plataforma Movistar Plus+, que cuenta con los derechos de emisión del evento. Sigue toda la actualidad del Balón de Oro, el minuto a minuto de la gala y la mejor cobertura en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.
